newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent crude takes a tumble, outright softer.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent crude takes a tumble, outright softer.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude took a tumble on Monday, pressured by limited European demand and unsold crude arriving in the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
A cargo loading in the October 10-12 range sold on Monday at an eight-cent discount to November Brent. This followed a deal on Friday at a six-cent premium to November.
Most traders saw little hope for a strong recovery on Brent, with no obvious buying in Europe. Some saw emerging interest from the U.S. as the arbitrage opened up.
"Brent is in the doldrums. We need some barrels to move out of the region for it to find a bottom.
"Maybe we are getting there. I see some interest today," one said.
A VLCC of Brent crude, arriving in the U.S. in the next few days, had at least one unsold cargo on board, traders said.
November IPE Brent crude recovered from the lows to trade down 19 cents on the day at $23.28 a barrel.
Talk was light on other North Sea barrels and premiums held steady.
Traders expected Ekofisk, with some mid-month cargoes remaining, to come under most pressure. There was little October Forties left and Oseberg had only end-month cargoes, they said.
"Overall we will probably see a few cents off Ekofisk and Oseberg but most of the others should hold," a refiner said.
Intermonth spreads came down with outright levels. Oct/Nov traded early at +30 cents, only to move late at +25 cents.
All three Brent dates were kept on Monday -- two by British Petroleum and one by Shell U.K. The three dates included one deferred from Friday's loading range.
